'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Iran–Saudi Arabia proxy conflict]]; [[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**[[2021 missile attacks in Saudi Arabia]]
***[[Saudi Arabia]] intercepts a [[ballistic missile]] attack over its capital [[Riyadh]] and bomb-laden [[unmanned combat aerial vehicle|drones]] targeting the southern province of [[Jazan Province|Jizan]], both of which were launched by [[Yemen]]'s [[Houthi movement|Houthi]] rebels backed by [[Iran]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/saudi-arabia-intercepts-missile-attack-capital-76155424 (ABC News)]
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]]
**[[Myanmar Police Force|Police]] launch the most extensive crackdown since the protests began, critically wounding a woman and detaining hundreds of people across the country. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-myanmar-politics/myanmar-police-launch-most-extensive-crackdown-one-woman-dead-media-say-idUSKBN2AR01I?il=0 (Reuters)]
**The [[State Administration Council|junta leaders]] fire Myanmar's [[List of current permanent representatives to the United Nations|Permanent Representative to the United Nations]] [[Kyaw Moe Tun]] after he called for their removal in a [[UN General Assembly]] meeting on Friday. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-56222987 (BBC News)]
*[[Kagara kidnapping]]
**All 42 people, including 27 students, who were kidnapped from a boarding school in [[Kagara, Niger State|Kagara]], [[Niger State]], [[Nigeria]], on February 17 are released by their captors. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/2/27/kidnappers-release-42-abducted-from-school-in-nigeria (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Wales]]
*****[[First Minister of Wales|First Minister]] [[Mark Drakeford]] announces that [[Wales]] will ease their [[COVID-19]] restrictions to allow households with an infant below the age of one to form a bubble with one other household. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-wales-56224669 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****The [[Government of Italy|government]] tightens restrictions in five [[Regions of Italy|region]]s in an attempt to reduce the spread of COVID-19. For the first time since January, [[Basilicata]] and [[Molise]] are moved into a lockdown, while [[Lombardy]], [[Piedmont]], and [[Marche]] are moved to stricter orange zones. [https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-health-coronavirus-italy-regions-idUKKBN2AR0EL (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Romania]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Moldova]]
****[[Romania]] donates 21,600 doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] to [[Moldova]] for use in their [[vaccination]] program which will begin next week with frontline [[health worker]]s. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2021-02-27/romania-ships-first-batch-of-astrazeneca-vaccine-to-moldova (U.S. News and World Report)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong]]
****[[Hong Kong]] receives a shipment of 585,000 doses of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech]] [[vaccine]]. [https://amp.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/health-environment/article/3123393/coronavirus-pfizer-biontech-vaccine-arrives-hong (''South China Morning Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] receives its first shipment of 300,000 doses of the [[Sinovac]] [[CoronaVac]] vaccine. [https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2021/02/669448/coronavac-covid-19-vaccine-arrives-beijing (''New Straits Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the State of Palestine]]
****The [[Palestinian National Authority]] announces new [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] restrictions in the [[West Bank]] for the next 12 days, which include the closure of universities, a ban on gatherings for weddings and funerals and nighttime restrictions on travel and non-essential commerce. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/02/27/world/middleeast/palestinians-west-bank-lockdown.html (''The New York Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****The [[Government of the Philippines|government]] extends the [[COVID-19 community quarantines in the Philippines|General Community Quarantine]] in [[Metro Manila]], [[Davao City]], and eight other areas until the end of March due to an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases. [https://news.abs-cbn.com/news/02/27/21/metro-manila-9-other-areas-to-remain-under-gcq-in-march-palace (ABS-CBN News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nebraska]], [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2]]
****[[Nebraska]] reports their first case of [[California]]'s B.1.429 variant in a man in his 60s in [[Lancaster County, Nebraska|Lancaster County]]. [https://journalstar.com/lifestyles/health-med-fit/health/lancaster-county-reports-first-case-of-california-coronavirus-variant/article_e247cc12-46e8-52f0-9a10-fefe130146c6.html (''The Lincoln Journal Star'')]  
***The [[Food and Drug Administration]] approves the single-dose [[Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine|Johnson & Johnson]] vaccine for [[Emergency Use Authorization|emergency use]] in the [[United States]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/feb/27/fda-approves-johnson-johnson-coronavirus-vaccine (''The Guardian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[COVID-19]]-related restrictions in [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] are eased in line with the rest of [[Australia]] after a recent outbreak was contained. Private gatherings of up to 30 people and public gatherings of up to 100 people are allowed, [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|masks]] will only be mandated in shopping centres and on public transport, and offices are allowed to return up to 75% of their workforce. [https://7news.com.au/lifestyle/health-wellbeing/victoria-covid-restrictions-eased-further-with-changes-to-gathering-and-mask-rules-weeks-after-snap-lockdown-c-2243824 (7 News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]]
***[[South Africa]] receives its second shipment of more than 80,000 doses of the Johnson & Johnson vaccine. [https://www.news24.com/amp/news24/southafrica/news/covid-19-second-batch-of-johnson-johnson-vaccine-arrives-on-saa-flight-from-belgium-20210227 (News24)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Corruption in Indonesia]]
**Indonesia's [[Corruption Eradication Commission|anti-corruption agency]] arrests [[South Sulawesi]] Governor [[Nurdin Abdullah]] and several other people for alleged [[corruption]] in [[Makassar]]. Abdullah's arrest came as a surprise to many with his track record as an anti-corruption champion. [https://jakartaglobe.id/news/anticorruption-champion-nabbed-by-kpk-when-sleeping (''Jakarta Globe'')]
*Iran's [[Sistan and Baluchestan Province]] has reported internet outages in the past week, following a series of violent clashes between protestors and the police. [https://www.voanews.com/middle-east/voa-news-iran/internet-disruption-reported-southeast-iran-amid-unrest (Voice of America)]
*[[Cuba]] approves its first [[animal welfare]] law after pressure from [[animal rights movement]] groups. The decree will regulate scientific experiments on animals, the handling of stray cats and dogs, and veterinarian practices in the country. Some civil society groups say the decree doesn't go far enough, as it doesn't outlaw [[animal sacrifice]] or [[cockfight]]ing. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-cuba-politics-animalrights/cuba-approves-animal-welfare-law-after-civil-society-pressure-idUSKBN2AR0GM?il=0 (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Armenian coup d'état attempt]], [[2020−2021 Armenian protests]]
**[[President of Armenia|President]] [[Armen Sarksyan]] refuses an order from [[Prime Minister of Armenia|Prime Minister]] [[Nikol Pashinyan]] to dismiss the [[Armed Forces of Armenia|military]]'s [[Chief of the General Staff (Armenia)|Chief of the General Staff]] [[Onik Gasparyan]], saying parts of the decree were in violation of the constitution. More than 15,000 protest in the capital [[Yerevan]] calling for Pashinyan to resign. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/armenias-president-refuses-order-dismiss-military-chief-76156042 (ABC News)]
